audit_notes: Model: through-thickness shear of a layer with exponentially graded shear modulus G(z) = (E_base/3) exp(-a z), a = ln(E_base/E_top) = ln(100) = 4.61, z = 0 at the anchored base, z = 1 at the surface; (G u')' = 0 gives u'' = a u'. Surface compliance c = u(1)/tau = 3 t (1 - e^-a)/(a E_top) = 3*4e-4*0.99/(4.61*2e5) = 1.29e-9 m/Pa. Kendall/ Brady thin-layer release criterion for a rigid fouler larger than the coating thickness: sigma_c = sqrt(2 Wa / c) -> sqrt(2*0.05/1.29e-9) = 8.8 kPa. Baseline: uniform silicone FR with E = 1 MPa, same thickness: c = 3 t/E = 1.2e-9 m/Pa -> sigma_c = 9.1 kPa. Expected gain (lower release stress) only ~3.5%: an exponential grading concentrates the compliance in the soft top ~20% of the thickness, so a 100x softer top buys almost nothing for large foulers; the benefit of a soft top applies mainly to foulers smaller than the soft-skin thickness (diatoms, early barnacle bases), which a 1D model does not resolve. To really lower sigma_c, the soft zone must be thick (e.g. linear or step grading with >50% soft volume). Note: measured barnacle release on silicone FR is 0.02-0.1 MPa because of cement penetration and interlock; the absolute sigma_c here is an idealisation, the ratio is what matters. Structural: DOPA-anchored base with 5 MPa adhesion strength is far above service loads (tau_w 50 Pa, fouling drag kPa), supporting multi-year adhesion; soft top (E = 0.2 MPa) has tear strength ~0.5-1 kN/m, vulnerable to abrasion. Dimensionless: E_base/E_top = 100, a = 4.61, Wa/(E_top t) = 6e-7.

performance_gain.label: Reduction of fouling release stress vs uniform FR

baseline_description: Uniform silicone foul-release coating, E = 1 MPa, same thickness
